hypothesis: A from-scratch randomized greedy exact-compatible construction can assemble seven disjoint 6-mark Golomb rulers within scope 111, providing an independent search family rather than retuning the published witness.
rationale: The DTS contract is a disjointness problem over 105 exact differences; sampling compatible rows directly tests whether greedy compatibility is sufficient at the target scope.
expected_information_gain: Quantifies row-pool compatibility, restart yield, and maximum number of assembled disjoint differences even if a full seven-row witness is not found.
method: At each of seven levels sample 3000 random normalized six-mark rows with scope <=111, retain internally Golomb rows disjoint from the used difference set, choose the best compatible candidate, and restart on failure.
metric: assembled row count and globally unique positive differences under scope <=111
metric_relation_to_true_objective: A complete seven-row assembly with 105 unique differences is exactly a valid DTS target; partial assemblies and pool compatibility are exploratory proxies.
kill_condition: Stop after three 20-second seeds or immediately on a complete independently validated scope-111 witness.
interpretation: No complete target witness was found. The greedy construction repeatedly assembled only four mutually disjoint Golomb rulers, reaching 60 unique differences before exhausting each restart's sampled compatible pool.
what_was_learned: Independent random row sampling has a severe compatibility bottleneck at scope 111; millions of sampled rows did not extend beyond four rows, so naive greedy assembly is not a high-value continuation without a better candidate-pool or backtracking strategy.
recommended_next_action: Pause naive random greedy search and test a compatibility-indexed exact-cover/backtracking method that can revisit earlier row choices.
